AirlineFlow: revised operating-leg and turnaround data

All four nested variants share the same revised five core tables. Origin and destination movements are present for each operating leg. Boarding sessions exist at the origin of both inbound and outbound flights; turnaround membership identifies the focal-airport departure. IDs are independent. Actual and receipt times differ.

Extraction requests

Current L05 pilot — Query Registry v6 / unchanged Gold event logs. The following 12 English requests are the exact model-input texts for the five-table pilot. The reference counts were obtained from the revised L05 SQLite; human semantic review remains pending. Case entity and reference counts are evaluator-only metadata, not part of the model input.

Q01 has been revised to ask about average boarding duration. Its output remains a session-level event log, not a scalar average. Q03 wording is pending final approval. All 12 requests use the five core tables; their reuse on larger nested variants requires checking that the intended scope and reference logs remain unchanged. Q01/Q11 share a reference log, as do Q06/Q12; Q09 is a movement-only subset of Q06.

Security queue time is screening start minus queue entry. Screening duration is completion minus screening start.

Sources and assumptions

This synthetic research schema draws on public descriptions of bookings, tickets, operating legs, ground preparation and baggage handling. It assumes access to linked airport screening and handling records. All timestamps are in KST.

  • EUROCONTROL A-CDM Specification
  • Postgres Pro Airlines schema
  • IATA baggage tracking guide

Movement reports include source, validation method and message format. Handling jobs include service provider, dispatch priority and work zone. The attributes are synthetic and informed by IATA AIDX and EUROCONTROL A-CDM. The kind and job_code columns still identify activities.

Passenger attributes and public models

The passengers table stores synthetic dates of birth, nationality codes and gender codes. Date of birth is a passenger attribute. The dataset records a single nationality, distinct from country of residence or document issuance. The local gender codes are MALE, FEMALE and UNKNOWN.

Public sourceHow the source informed the dataset
Postgres Pro Airlines (2017 schema family)This demo database defines bookings, tickets and ticket_flights. The demo stores passenger data in tickets. AirlineFlow uses a separate passengers table with internal synthetic passenger IDs.
Amadeus booking exampleThe booking API example places dateOfBirth and gender on the traveller and nationality on the travel document. AirlineFlow stores nationality on the passenger record.
EUROCONTROL A-CDMA-CDM informs the distinction between boarding, aircraft readiness and departure. The inbound_id and outbound_id fields link legs operated by the same aircraft. Request T combines inbound LAND and IN, ground handling, and outbound OUT and AIR. The example uses completed turnarounds with no aircraft swaps.

The dataset simplifies fares, payments, seats, travel document history, rebooking, diversions and repeated boarding sessions. Each flight contains a sample of passenger and baggage records. Flight-level closure times come from dedicated handling records.
